title: Trace Sampling Replay Inspector with Dashboard Drilldowns
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Ship a lightweight service (Trace Sampling Replay Inspector) that lets SREs and engineers: 1) capture sampled and representative unsampled traces, 2) replay partial trace windows against a sandboxed Tempo backend, and 3) pivot from a latency/error spike in the Console dashboard into an automated drilldown that pre-populates the replay and sampling filters.

Scope:
- An ingest shim that taps OTLP spans and copies a small percentage of unsampled or low-sampling-rate traffic into a replay store.
- A replay engine that can materialize partial traces (time-window or span-range) and forward them to a dedicated sandbox Tempo instance with compatibility tweaks (span envelope, trace IDs, and timestamp normalization).
- Console dashboard integration: new Drilldown action on latency/error charts that opens the inspector with suggested filters (service, span name, percentiles, timeframe) and a one-click replay run.
- Safety & privacy: masking pipeline to redact PII in copied spans and per-team opt-out controls.
- Performance constraints: stream-copy must add <1.5% CPU and <2ms tail latency to instrumented services when using sidecar mode.

Non-goals: full trace retention, replacing primary Tempo ingestion, or exhaustive sampling policy UI (those are separate initiatives).

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow: Console -> Drilldown -> Inspector -> Sandbox Tempo replay (green path demonstrated in e2e test).
- Replay fidelity: timestamps and parent-child ordering preserved for the partial trace window >= 95% of fields (exclusions: known vendor-only metadata).
- Controlled overhead verified on two benchmark services (api-gateway, model-ingest).
- Runbook + rollback steps documented for oncall.

Implementation notes:
- Use existing OTLP relay to fork spans into a local replay Kafka topic with a fixed retention of 72 hours.
- Replay runner pulls events in-order and posts to sandbox Tempo via gRPC OTLP with envelope translation for legacy tags.
- Add a lightweight sidecar mode (go-based) for high-cardinality services and an aggregator mode for lower-cardinality infra.
- Provide a Console React component for the Drilldown button and an API endpoint that returns suggested filters based on histogram peaks.

Observability metrics to ship: replay_attempts, replay_success_rate, replay_latency_histogram, sidecar_cpu_delta, sidecar_mem_delta, replayed_spans_count, redaction_failures.

Docs/artifacts: design doc: https://docs.internal.redwood/dev/observability/trace-replay-design (draft), prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 (WIP).
comments: 2026-02-16 - Ava Martinez: Kicked off design sync with Console and SRE. Agreed on replay sandbox approach rather than live re-ingestion. Action: produce CONTRAINTS table for performance baseline.
2026-02-20 - Ravi Shah: Spike complete - sidecar adds ~0.9% CPU on api-gateway with 5k RPS test, latencies within targets. Pushed initial PoC branch (PR link above).
2026-02-23 - Priya Nair (SRE): Reviewed privacy/redaction approach. Suggested adding per-team opt-out flag at collector-level. Added label 'needs-security-review'.
2026-02-26 - Design review: Console team approved Drilldown UX mockups. Next: API contract for suggested filters and replay trigger.
2026-03-01 - Ravi Shah: Implemented replay-runner state machine and simple retry semantics. Preparing integration tests for partial-trace ordering.
next_steps: Finalize redaction library choice (prose/pseudonymize), add E2E tests that validate ordering and reparenting, and schedule a canary with api-gateway in staging. Coordinate with Console to wire Drilldown action to the new /inspector/replay endpoint.
postmortem_runbook: If replay spikes or causes backpressure: 1) disable sidecar fork via runtime flag, 2) flip collector to drop-to-disk mode, 3) pause replay topic consumers, 4) run quick analyzers on last known good snapshot and alert oncall. Playbook in docs link in description.
